explain.say: Imagine you take a photo of a sunset on a beach in Goa. Your phone cannot keep the real sky, only numbers. So how does a picture become numbers? Let us zoom right in. Look at the board: here is your whole photo.

explain.say: Zoom in close and the smooth picture breaks into tiny squares in a grid. Each square is called a pixel, short for picture element. A phone photo has millions of them. Have you ever zoomed so far that a photo looked blocky?

explain.say: Here is the trick: every colour on a screen is a mix of red, green and blue light, called RGB. Each gets a number from 0 to 255. Orange might be red 255, green 140, blue 0. White is all three at 255. What do you think black is?

explain.say: Yes, black is 0, 0, 0! Each of those numbers is 8 bits, so one pixel uses 24 bits. Wow fact: that gives 256 times 256 times 256, which is over 16 million colours, and a 12 megapixel photo holds 36 million numbers. Brilliant zooming!

faq.a: A pixel is one tiny square of colour in a digital picture. Pictures are grids of millions of pixels, so small that your eye blends them into a smooth image.
asks: Why do photos look blocky when zoomed?

faq.a: RGB stands for red, green and blue. Screens mix these three colours of light, each with a number from 0 to 255, to make every colour you see.

faq.q: How does a computer store a picture?
faq.a: It splits the picture into a grid of pixels and stores each pixel colour as three numbers, red, green and blue. Each number is saved as 8 bits.
asks: How are images stored as binary?

faq.a: A megapixel is one million pixels. A 12 megapixel camera takes photos made of about 12 million pixels, for example 4000 across by 3000 down.
asks: Do more megapixels mean better photos?

faq.q: How many colours can a screen show?
faq.a: With 256 levels each of red, green and blue, a screen can show 256 times 256 times 256 colours, which is 16,777,216, more than 16 million.
asks: How many colours are in 24-bit colour?

facts: With 8 bits each for red, green and blue, there are 256 × 256 × 256 = 16,777,216 possible colours.
One megapixel is one million pixels.

quiz.say: A pixel has red 255, green 255 and blue 255. What colour is it?
quiz.why: All three lights at full brightness mix to make white light.

wrong.1: Black is 0, 0, 0: all the lights off.
wrong.2: Brown needs much less green and blue than red.

quiz.say: Why does a photo look blocky when you zoom in a lot?

options.show: You can see the separate pixels
options.say: You can see the separate pixels

quiz.why: Every picture is a grid of single-colour squares, and zooming makes them big enough to see.

wrong.1: Every digital photo does this, even from a perfect camera.
wrong.2: The colours stay the same; the squares just get bigger.
